games.title: Baraf Pani (Ice Water)
games.description: A freeze tag variant where tagged players become 'frozen' (baraf) and must stand still until a teammate touches them to 'melt' (pani) and free them.
games.occasion: School breaks, park play, family gatherings
howToPlay: Step 1: One or more players are chosen as taggers.
Step 2: When a tagger touches a player, that player becomes 'frozen' (baraf) and must stand still.
Step 3: Frozen players cannot move until a free teammate touches them.
Step 4: The touching teammate 'melts' (pani) them, allowing them to run again.
Step 5: Taggers try to freeze all players.
Step 6: Free players try to rescue frozen teammates.
Step 7: Game ends when all players are frozen.
Step 8: New taggers are chosen for next round.
Step 9: Develops teamwork and strategic movement.
Step 10: Popular in schools and neighborhoods.

games.title: Desi Kushti (Traditional Wrestling)
games.description: Traditional South Asian wrestling practiced in akharas (training pits). Once as popular as cricket, with rich history of champions and regional competitions.
howToPlay: Step 1: Wrestlers train in akharas under experienced coaches (pehelwans).
Step 2: Before independence, 100-150 akharas existed in Multan alone.
Step 3: Matches (dangal) are held in sandy pits.
Step 4: Wrestlers apply oil to their bodies for flexibility.
Step 5: They face each other and attempt to pin opponent's shoulders to ground.
Step 6: Various grappling techniques and holds are used.
Step 7: Matches continue until one wrestler achieves a pin or submission.
Step 8: Referees ensure fair play and declare winners.
Step 9: Winners receive prizes and gain reputation.
Step 10: Traditional wrestling declined after 1980s but still practiced.

games.title: Gulli Danda
games.description: Traditional stick game played across Pakistan, known by various regional names. Considered the predecessor of modern bat-and-ball games.
howToPlay: Step 1: A small hole is dug in the ground or a circle drawn.
Step 2: Place the gulli across the hole with one end raised.
Step 3: Use the danda to flick the gulli into the air.
Step 4: Strike the airborne gulli with the danda to hit it far.
Step 5: Fielders try to catch the gulli before it lands.
Step 6: If caught, batter is out; if not, measure distance using danda lengths.
Step 7: Batter scores points equal to number of danda lengths.
Step 8: Players take turns batting and fielding.
Step 9: The player with highest total distance wins.
Step 10: Regional variations exist across Pakistan.

games.title: Kabaddi (Pakistan Style)
games.description: Pakistan's version of kabaddi, known as 'Circle Kabaddi' played in a circular field. One of the most popular traditional sports with passionate followings and international competitions.
howToPlay: Step 1: Played in a circular field instead of rectangular court.
Step 2: Two teams of eight players occupy opposite halves.
Step 3: Raider enters opponent's half chanting 'kabaddi' without taking breath.
Step 4: Raider attempts to tag defenders and return to their half.
Step 5: Defenders try to tackle the raider.
Step 6: Points scored for successful tags.
Step 7: Circle kabaddi allows more players and different tackling techniques.
Step 8: Teams alternate raiders throughout the game.
Step 9: Pakistan has strong kabaddi tradition with world-class players.
Step 10: Major tournaments held during national holidays.

games.title: Kancha (Marbles)
games.description: Classic marble game played across Pakistan, known as Kancha or Rumi. Children collect and trade colorful glass marbles, competing in skill-based challenges.
howToPlay: Step 1: Draw a circle on flat ground.
Step 2: Each player places several marbles inside the circle.
Step 3: Players take turns shooting their shooter marble from outside the circle.
Step 4: Flick the shooter with thumb to knock marbles out.
Step 5: Keep any marbles knocked out of the circle.
Step 6: If shooter stays inside, player continues; if not, turn passes.
Step 7: Game continues until all marbles are cleared.
Step 8: Player with most marbles collected wins.
Step 9: Special marbles are prized and traded.
Step 10: Advanced techniques include backspin and curve shots.

games.title: Ludo (Desi Version)
games.description: Pakistani version of the classic board game, descended from the ancient Indian game Pachisi. Played with cowrie shells instead of dice in traditional settings.
howToPlay: Step 1: Players choose colored pieces and place them in the starting area.
Step 2: Throw cowrie shells to determine moves (number of shells opening up determines count).
Step 3: Move pieces around the board according to the throw.
Step 4: Landing on an opponent's square sends their piece back to start.
Step 5: Safe squares protect pieces from capture.
Step 6: To enter the home column, piece must land exactly on the entrance square.
Step 7: All pieces must reach the center to win.
Step 8: Strategy involves deciding which pieces to move and when.
Step 9: The first player to get all pieces home wins.
Step 10: Traditional version uses cowrie shells instead of modern dice.

games.title: Oonch Neech (High Low)
games.description: A popular tag game where players are safe only when on elevated surfaces (oonch) and vulnerable when on ground level (neech). Tests agility and quick thinking.
games.occasion: School breaks, family gatherings, casual play
howToPlay: Step 1: Designate one player as the denner (catcher).
Step 2: Establish that elevated surfaces (walls, benches, stairs) are 'safe zones'.
Step 3: Ground level is 'unsafe' where players can be tagged.
Step 4: Players run and dodge, jumping onto elevated surfaces to avoid tagging.
Step 5: The denner tries to tag players when they are on ground level.
Step 6: Tagged players become denners or are eliminated.
Step 7: Players cannot stay on safe zones indefinitely.
Step 8: Game continues until all players are tagged.
Step 9: Last player tagged wins and becomes denner for next round.
Step 10: Develops agility, speed, and strategic movement.

games.title: Pittu Garam (Seven Stones)
games.description: Popular street game where players knock down a pile of seven stones with a ball, then try to rebuild while avoiding being hit by opponents.
howToPlay: Step 1: Stack seven flat stones in a pile.
Step 2: One team throws the ball to knock down the stone pile.
Step 3: The throwing team tries to rebuild the pile while opponents throw the ball to hit them.
Step 4: If hit by the ball, that player is out.
Step 5: The rebuilding team must avoid being hit while stacking stones.
Step 6: If the pile is successfully rebuilt, the team scores points.
Step 7: Teams then switch roles.
Step 8: The game requires speed, accuracy, and teamwork.
Step 9: Players can catch the ball to eliminate throwers.
Step 10: Multiple rounds determine the winner.

games.title: Stapoo (Hopscotch)
games.description: Pakistani version of hopscotch, primarily played by girls. Players hop through numbered boxes while kicking a flat stone, often accompanied by traditional rhymes.
equipment: Chalk or stick to draw boxes
howToPlay: Step 1: Draw a hopscotch grid with numbered boxes on the ground.
Step 2: Players toss a flat stone into the first box.
Step 3: Hop on one foot through the boxes, avoiding the box with the stone.
Step 4: Kick the stone to the next box while hopping.
Step 5: Continue until reaching the end and turn back.
Step 6: If successful, toss stone to next box and repeat.
Step 7: Player loses turn if stone lands on a line, both feet touch ground, or balance is lost.
Step 8: Player who completes all boxes first wins.
Step 9: Advanced players add complex patterns and faster movements.
Step 10: Singing often accompanies the game.
